title: Agents that share a seat and call irc_name with no name all get the same name
description:
## Problem
When several agents have the same seat (same machine, same folder, no tmux pane and no terminal, for example three CLI windows without a console started in one folder), a new MCP session starts with the name remembered for that seat, and irc_name with no argument returns that same name (chat.SetName keeps the seat's name). All of them then share one name unless each passes an explicit name.

Since c11acf5 the hook side is solved (each hook is told apart by its CLI session id and the irc_name result), but only once the names differ.

## Wanted
An agent that calls irc_name with no name gets its own name when another live session already uses the seat's remembered name.

## Sketch (keep it small)
In the daemon, when a session is created for a seat whose remembered name is held by another live session with a different shim process id, start the session with no name instead of the remembered one. irc_name with no argument then generates a fresh name. The single-agent restart case (the old session is gone or has the same parent process) keeps the remembered name as today.

## Tests
- unit (internal/daemon): two live sessions, same seat, different process ids: the second starts unnamed and irc_name gives it a new name; the first keeps its name.
- unit: one session ends (or the daemon restarts) and a new one on the seat gets the remembered name back.
- e2e: extend TestAgentsThatShareASeatAndAParentAreToldApartByTheirSession with a variant where the agents call irc_name with no argument.

## Out of scope
Any change to the seat format or to the four tools.
notes: Landed 7c0a1bc. Done differently from the sketch: liveness comes from a watch connection each shim holds open (GET /v1/watch), not from process ids, because several CLIs run their MCP servers under one shared parent and a killed shim sends no goodbye. Also added: a seat shared by different names is skipped when resolving a hook.
close_reason: Completed in 7c0a1bc; gate green locally (gofumpt, vet, golangci-lint 0 issues, go test -race incl. the new e2e scenario).

title: chat: the rules for naming, sending, reading and hook delivery (core.Chat)
description:
## Goal

The rule layer: everything `mairc` decides about naming, sending, reading and hook delivery, implementing
`core.Chat` on top of a `core.Store`.

## Files you own

`internal/chat/*.go` (package `chat`) and its tests. Nothing else.

## Build against the contract, not against other packages

Everything you need is in `internal/core/core.go`: `Settings`, `Message`, `Agent`, `Kind`, `Clock`, `Store`,
`Chat`, `MaxRecipients` and the `Err...` values. **Write a fake `core.Store` in your test file** (an in-memory
implementation of the interface, about 150 lines); do not import `internal/store`. Name rules come from
`internal/names` if it has landed; if it has not, define the two functions you need as unexported variables
(`validName`, `generateName`) with the behaviour below and swap them when `names` lands:
valid = `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,23}$` and not `room`, `all`, `system`, `irc`; generated = colour+animal+digit.

```go
package chat

// New returns the rule layer. rnd(n) returns a number in [0, n) and feeds name generation.
func New(store core.Store, clock core.Clock, settings core.Settings, rnd func(n int) int) *Service
// *Service implements core.Chat.
```

## Rules

**Text.** Before any check, a message text is cleaned: every run of control characters (including `\n`, `\r`,
`\t`) becomes one space, then surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Length is counted in Unicode code points
(`utf8.RuneCountInString`) of the cleaned text.

**SetName(want, seat).**
- `want == ""`: if the seat already has a name, return it; else generate one (free in the store) and bind it.
- otherwise normalize (trim, lowercase), check validity (`core.ErrNameInvalid`), and `UpsertAgent(name, seat)`;
  `core.ErrNameTaken` passes through.
- Setting the name an agent already has in that seat succeeds and changes nothing.

**Send(from, to, text).** In this order; the first failure is returned:
1. `from == ""` → `core.ErrNoName`.
2. cleaned text empty → `core.ErrEmpty`.
3. Room (`len(to) == 0`): `!PublicEnabled` → `core.ErrRoomOff`.
   Private: `!PrivateEnabled` → `core.ErrPMOff`.
4. Length over `MaxPublicLen` / `MaxPrivateLen` → an error that `errors.Is(err, core.ErrTooLong)` and whose text
   is exactly `too long <len>/<max>` (for example `too long 300/256`).
5. Private only: normalize and de-duplicate `to`; more than `core.MaxRecipients` (16) →
   `core.ErrTooManyRecipients`. Any name that is not a known agent, or is the sender itself → an error that
   `errors.Is(err, core.ErrUnknown)` with text `unknown: a,b` (the offending names in the order given).
6. Cooldown: if the sender's last send of that kind is less than the cooldown ago → an error that
   `errors.Is(err, core.ErrCooldown)` with text `cooldown <n>s`, `n` = whole seconds left, rounded up, at least 1.
   A cooldown of 0 never refuses. Room and private cooldowns are independent. A private message to several
   agents is one send.
7. Store it (`InsertRoom` or `InsertPM`), then prune (`Store.Prune` with the settings), then update the
   in-memory state below.

**Read(name, n).** `core.ErrNoName` for `""`. Returns the unread private messages (oldest first, now read), then
the last `n` room lines (oldest first). `n <= 0` or `n > MaxRoomLines` means `MaxRoomLines`. It also sets the
agent's room cursor to the newest room message id and clears its in-memory unread flag, so a hook does not
deliver again what the agent just read.

**Who().** Names seen within `KeepHours`, most recent first, at most 50.

**HookEvent(name).** This is the hot path (it runs after every tool call of every agent).
- Keep in memory, behind one mutex: per agent `privateEvents`, `roomEvents`, `hasUnreadPM`, `roomCursor`; and
  globally `maxRoomID`. Load an agent's entry from the store the first time it is seen
  (`Store.HasUnreadPM`, `Agent.RoomCursor`); load `maxRoomID` once at `New`.
- Each call adds one to both counters. Then:
  - if `privateEvents >= CheckPrivateEvery`: reset it; if `hasUnreadPM`, take `Store.UnreadPMs` and clear the flag;
  - if `roomEvents >= CheckRoomEvery`: reset it; if `maxRoomID > roomCursor`, take
    `Store.RoomSince(roomCursor, name, MaxRoomLines)`, then set the cursor to `maxRoomID` (in memory and with
    `Store.SetRoomCursor`).
- Return private messages first, then room lines. **When nothing is taken, return `nil, nil` without calling any
  store method.** `""` → `nil, nil` (an unnamed agent gets nothing; no error).
- `Send` updates this state: a room send raises `maxRoomID`; a private send sets `hasUnreadPM` for each recipient.
- Every call also records the agent as seen, at most once a minute per agent (`Store.Touch`), never on the
  nothing-due path more often than that.

**Reload(s).** Swap the settings under the mutex. Counters keep their values.

## Tests (fake store, fake clock)

- every `Send` rule above in order, with the exact error texts: `empty`, `room off`, `pm off`, `too long 300/256`,
  `too many recipients (max 16)`, `unknown: bob,carol`, `cooldown 42s`, `no name: call irc_name`;
- cleaning: `"a\n\tb  "` is stored as `"a b"`; a 256-rune text of multi-byte characters is accepted, 257 refused;
- cooldown boundaries with the fake clock (59 s refused with `cooldown 1s`, 60 s accepted; 0 disables it); room
  and private are independent; one multi-recipient message is one send;
- `SetName`: generate, keep on repeat, invalid, taken, rename in the same seat;
- `Read`: private first then room, marks read, caps `n`, moves the cursor;
- `HookEvent`: with the defaults a private message is delivered on the next event and a room line only on every
  10th event; with `CheckPrivateEvery=3` on the 3rd; the agent's own room lines are never delivered; a message
  delivered by a hook is not delivered again; `Read` after a hook delivery shows the room line as history and no
  private message;
- **the zero-cost assertion:** the fake store counts calls; 1,000 `HookEvent` calls for an agent with nothing due
  make **zero** store calls beyond the at-most-once-a-minute `Touch`;
- `Reload` changes limits immediately;
- a `-race` test with 8 goroutines mixing `Send`, `Read` and `HookEvent`.
- `BenchmarkHookEventEmpty` (target: under 200 ns/op, 0 allocations; report the number in the close reason).

## Not in this bead

Rendering lines for the agent (`core.Message.Line` exists), JSON, HTTP, MCP, the database itself.

## Working rules (the same for every bead)

- **Project in three lines:** `mairc` is a tiny chat system for coding agents, served as an MCP server. A
  background daemon owns one SQLite file; agents reach it through a stdio shim, Streamable HTTP, and a hook that
  prints nothing when there is nothing to read. One public room, private messages, nothing else.
- **No scope creep.** Build exactly what this bead says. If something seems missing, write it in the bead's notes
  and ask; do not add features, flags, settings or dependencies.
- **Toolchain:** Go 1.27.4. `export PATH=$HOME/sdk/go1.27.4/bin:$HOME/go/bin:$PATH`. Build with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
- **Contract:** `internal/core/core.go` holds the shared types and interfaces. Use them as they are. Do not edit
  that file unless this bead says so.
- **Rust-port readiness:** standard library first; the only third-party dependency allowed in the whole project is
  `modernc.org/sqlite`, and only in `internal/store`. No reflection tricks, no code generation, no global mutable
  state, no `init()` side effects, no panics for control flow. Errors are values with stable short texts.
- **Tests:** table-driven, `testing` only (no assertion libraries), a fake clock, temporary directories, no
  sleeps, no network beyond loopback. Every user-visible string named in this bead is asserted verbatim.
- **Before you push:** `gofumpt -l . && go vet ./... && golangci-lint run && go test -race -count=1 ./...`, all
  clean. If `.golangci.yml` is not in the repository yet, run `golangci-lint run` with its defaults.
- **Stay in your files.** Touch only the paths listed under "Files you own". Remove the `.gitkeep` in a directory
  when you add its first real file.
- **Beads:** claim with `br update <id> --claim --actor "<model> (<your name>)"`, close with

## Goal

One command that runs every check, the lint configuration, and a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the same
command on every push and pull request.

## Files you own

`Taskfile.yml`, `.golangci.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Nothing else. No Go code.

## `Taskfile.yml` (the `task` runner is installed at `~/go/bin/task`)

Tasks, each a thin wrapper so agents and CI run the same thing:

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| `fmt` | `gofumpt -l -w .` |
| `fmt:check` | fail if `gofumpt -l .` prints anything |
| `vet` | `go vet ./...` |
| `lint` | `golangci-lint run` |
| `test` | `go test -race -count=1 ./...` |
| `build` | `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w" -o bin/mairc ./cmd/mairc` |
| `vuln` | `govulncheck ./...` |
| `check` | `fmt:check`, `vet`, `lint`, `test`, `build` in that order (this is the pre-push command) |

`bin/` is already in `.gitignore`.

## `.golangci.yml` (golangci-lint v2 format, `version: "2"`)

- Enable, on top of the defaults: `errcheck`, `govet`, `staticcheck`, `ineffassign`, `unused`, `gosec`,
  `revive`, `errorlint`, `bodyclose`, `noctx`, `contextcheck`, `fatcontext`, `perfsprint`, `prealloc`,
  `unconvert`, `misspell`, `gocritic`, `nilerr`, `sqlclosecheck`, `rowserrcheck`.

  - `depguard`: outside `internal/store`, importing `modernc.org/sqlite` or `database/sql` is denied; importing

  weaken the rule: list the findings in the bead's notes and tell the owner of that package.

- Triggers: `push` to `main`, and `pull_request`.

  install `gofumpt`, `golangci-lint` v2 and `task` (pin versions), then `task check`, then `task vuln`.
- `permissions: contents: read`. A `concurrency` group per ref that cancels superseded runs. Job timeout 15
  minutes. Pin every action to a full commit SHA with the version in a comment.
- No release, no publishing, no secrets.

- `task check` passes locally on the current `main`, and fails when you introduce (and then remove) a formatting
  error, a vet error and a failing test: say in the close reason that you tried each.

  `act -n` (installed at `~/go/bin/act`) as a dry run.

title: daemon: the HTTP server (MCP Streamable HTTP, hook, reload, status) and lifecycle
description:
## Goal

`mairc daemon`: the one long-running process. It owns the database, serves MCP over Streamable HTTP, answers the
hook endpoint, and prunes old messages.

## Files you own

`internal/daemon/*.go` (package `daemon`), its tests, and `docs/protocol.md` (the HTTP section). Nothing else.

## What you build on (all landed before you start; this bead depends on them)

- `internal/config`: `ResolvePaths`, `EnsureHome`, `Load`, `Validate`, `ReadToken`, `Paths{Home, Config, DB, Token, Log, PID}`.
- `internal/store`: `store.Open(path) (*store.Store, error)` implementing `core.Store`.
- `internal/chat`: `chat.New(store, clock, settings, rnd) *chat.Service` implementing `core.Chat`
  (`SetName`, `NameForSeat`, `Send`, `Read`, `Who`, `HookEvent`, `Reload`).
- `internal/mcp`: `mcp.New(name, version, tools) *mcp.Server` and
  `(*Server).Handle(ctx, *core.Session, msg []byte) []byte` (nil for a notification).
- `internal/tools`: `tools.All(chat) []core.Tool`.

## API to implement

```go
package daemon

// Options configure a daemon. Zero values mean production defaults.
type Options struct {
	Paths   config.Paths
	Version string
	Clock   core.Clock        // default: wall clock
	Logf    func(format string, args ...any) // default: writes to Paths.Log
}

// Run starts the daemon and blocks until ctx is cancelled or a fatal error. It returns nil on a clean stop and
// also when another daemon already holds the listen address ("already running").
func Run(ctx context.Context, o Options) error

// Handler returns the HTTP handler alone, for tests (httptest) and for the end-to-end test.
func Handler(chat core.Chat, mcpServer *mcp.Server, token, version string, reload func() error, clock core.Clock) http.Handler
```

## Start-up (in `Run`)

1. `EnsureHome`; load and validate settings (an invalid file is a fatal error naming the key).
2. Token: if `Paths.Token` is missing, create it with 32 random bytes as 64 hex characters, mode 0600.
3. Listen on `settings.Listen`. If the address is in use and `GET /healthz` there answers `ok`, log
   `already running` and return nil. Any other listen error is fatal.
4. Open the store, build chat, tools and the MCP server (server name `mairc`), write `Paths.PID`.
5. Serve. Start one ticker: every 60 s call `Store.Prune(now, KeepHours, KeepMessages)`.
6. On `ctx` cancel (the caller wires SIGINT/SIGTERM): stop accepting, let in-flight requests finish for at most
   2 s, stop the ticker, close the store, remove the pid file.

Server timeouts: `ReadHeaderTimeout` 2 s, `ReadTimeout` 5 s, `WriteTimeout` 5 s, `IdleTimeout` 60 s.
Request bodies are limited to 64 KiB (`http.MaxBytesReader`); larger → 413.

## Endpoints

Every endpoint except `/healthz` requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; compare with
`subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`; otherwise `401` with an empty body.

### `GET /healthz`
`200`, body `ok`.

### `POST /mcp` (MCP Streamable HTTP, JSON responses only)
- Body: one JSON-RPC message. Pass it to `mcpServer.Handle` with the caller's session.
- Response for a request: `200`, `Content-Type: application/json`, the bytes returned.
  For a notification (`Handle` returns nil): `202`, empty body.
- `GET` and `DELETE` on `/mcp`: `405` (no server-initiated stream is offered).
- **Sessions** (in memory, a map behind a mutex):
  - On an `initialize` request, create a session with a random 128-bit hex id and return it in the
    `Mcp-Session-Id` response header.
  - Later requests carry `Mcp-Session-Id`; an unknown id → `404` (the client re-initializes, as the MCP
    specification says). A non-initialize request without the header → `400`.
  - A session holds a `core.Session{Name, Seat}` and an optional process id.
  - Headers a shim adds on `initialize`: `X-Mairc-Seat` (the seat) and `X-Mairc-Pid` (a positive integer). Store
    both on the session. If the seat has a remembered name (`chat.NameForSeat`), set `Session.Name` to it.
  - Sessions idle for more than 24 h are dropped by the retention ticker.

### `POST /v1/hook`
- Body: `{"pids":[int,...],"seat":"...","name":"...","event":"..."}` (every field optional).
- Resolve the agent name, the first that applies: a non-empty `name`; the name of the session whose stored
  process id equals one of `pids`, tried in the order given (nearest ancestor first); `chat.NameForSeat(seat)`.
  A process id stored on live sessions with **different** names is ambiguous (two agents started by one parent
  process, as in the end-to-end test) and is skipped, so resolution falls through to the next pid or the seat.
  Keep a `pid -> names` index in memory so this lookup needs no scan.
- Named: `msgs, _ := chat.HookEvent(ctx, name)`. No messages → `204`. Messages → `200`,
  `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, body = each `Message.Line()` joined by `\n`, no trailing newline.
- Not named: `204`, except when `event` is `SessionStart`: `200` with the body `irc: call irc_name to join`.
- Any internal error → `204` (the hook must stay silent) and a log line.
- This is the hot path. Do not allocate a session, log, or touch the database when nothing is due.

### `POST /v1/reload`
Re-load and validate the settings file and call `chat.Reload`. `204` on success; `400` with the error text when
the file is invalid (the old settings stay in force).

### `GET /v1/status`
`200` JSON `{"version":"...","uptime_s":N,"agents":N,"sessions":N}` (`agents` = names seen within `KeepHours`).

## Logging

One line per start, stop, fatal error, reload and internal error, to `Paths.Log` (append, 0600).
No per-request logging. Never log message bodies or the token.

## Tests (use `Handler` with `httptest`, a temporary home, a fake clock and the real store, chat, tools and mcp)

- auth: missing or wrong token → 401 on each endpoint; `/healthz` needs none;
- `/mcp`: initialize returns a session id; `tools/list` works with it; unknown id → 404; missing id → 400;
  a notification → 202; `GET` → 405; a 65 KiB body → 413;
- two sessions: A names itself, sends to the room and privately to B; B's `/v1/hook` (resolved by pid, by seat,
  and by explicit name, one test each) returns the lines once and then 204;
- an unnamed caller gets 204, and the `SessionStart` line exactly once per call with that event;
- the seat remembers the name: a new session with the same `X-Mairc-Seat` already has `Session.Name`;
- `/v1/reload` applies a changed `max_public_len`; an invalid file answers 400 and keeps the old value;
- `/v1/status` shape;
- `Run`: starts, serves, stops cleanly on cancel, removes the pid file; a second `Run` on the same address returns
  nil with `already running`;
- `docs/protocol.md` documents exactly these endpoints (status codes, headers, bodies) for a future port.
- `BenchmarkHookEmpty` over `httptest`: report ns/op and allocs in the close reason.

## Not in this bead

The `mairc` command line (the `cli` bead calls `Run`), the shim, the hook client, installing a system service.

## Working rules (the same for every bead)

```sh
go install github.com/horus14-wq/microagentIRC/cmd/mairc@latest   # or build: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o mairc ./cmd/mairc
mairc install            # registers the MCP server and the hooks for Claude Code (user scope)
mairc install --print    # other agent CLIs: prints the MCP command and the hook command to paste
```

Other agent CLIs: MCP server command `mairc stdio`; hook command `mairc hook --client plain` on session start,
on each user prompt and after each tool call. HTTP transport: `http://127.0.0.1:4747/mcp` with header

`mairc hook --name <your name>`.

**The four tools** (names, arguments and results exactly as served):

| Tool | Arguments | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `irc_name` | `name?` | `you are greenfox1` — omit `name` to be given one |
| `irc_send` | `text`, `to?` | `sent` — no `to` = the room; `to="a,b"` = private to those agents |
| `irc_read` | `n?` | unread private messages, then the last `n` room lines; `nothing new` |
| `irc_who` | — | names seen recently, space-separated |

Lines look like `pm greenfox1: text` and `room reddog7: text`.

**Rules an agent must know.**
- Call `irc_name` once before anything else; the name is remembered for the same terminal or tmux pane.
- Names: 2–24 characters, `a-z 0-9 _ -`, a letter first.
- Messages are one line, at most 256 characters by default.
- Cooldown: one room message per 60 s and one private message per 60 s by default. A private message to several
  agents counts once.
- New messages arrive on their own through the hook: private ones at the next event, room lines every 10th
  event. Do **not** poll with `irc_read`; use it only when you want history or were told to.
- Errors are short and literal: `cooldown 42s`, `too long 300/256`, `empty`, `unknown: bob`, `pm off`,
  `room off`, `too many recipients (max 16)`, `no name: call irc_name`, `name taken`.
- Messages are kept for 24 hours and at most 1000 of them, by default.

**Settings** (`mairc config`, `mairc config get <key>`, `mairc config set <key> <value>`):

| Key | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `max_private_len` | 1–999 | 256 |
| `max_public_len` | 1–999 | 256 |
| `max_room_lines` | 1–100 | 10 |
| `private_enabled` | true/false | true |
| `public_enabled` | true/false | true |
| `private_cooldown_s` | 0–86400 | 60 |
| `public_cooldown_s` | 0–86400 | 60 |
| `keep_messages` | 1–1000000 | 1000 |
| `keep_hours` | 1–8760 | 24 |
| `check_private_every` | 1–1000 events | 1 |
| `check_room_every` | 1–1000 events | 10 |
| `listen` | loopback `host:port` | `127.0.0.1:4747` |
| `hook_timeout_ms` | 50–5000 | 300 |

**Commands:** `mairc daemon` (runs in the foreground; `mairc stdio` starts it when needed), `mairc stdio`,
`mairc hook [--client claude|plain] [--event E] [--name N]`, `mairc config`, `mairc install [--scope
user|project] [--print] [--uninstall]`, `mairc status`, `mairc version`.

**Files:** `~/.local/share/mairc/` (or `$MAIRC_HOME`): `config.json`, `mairc.db`, `token`, `daemon.log`.

  to 0 unless the test is about cooldowns.

  exits 0 within 3 s.
- An "agent" is a child process `mairc stdio` with `MAIRC_SEAT=<name of the test agent>` in its environment, to
  which the test writes JSON-RPC lines and from which it reads response lines.
- A "hook" is a run of `mairc hook --client plain` with the same `MAIRC_SEAT`, capturing stdout.
  (Both test agents are children of the test process, so their process id is ambiguous to the daemon and it
  resolves each hook by its seat. That is the intended behaviour, not a workaround.)

   call `irc_name` with no name: both get a generated name matching `^[a-z]+[a-z]+[0-9]+$`, different from each
   other. A sends `hello room` to the room and `hi` privately to B. B's hook prints exactly
   `irc:\npm <A>: hi\n`. B's hook run again prints nothing.
2. **The zero-token path.** With nothing new, 50 hook runs for B print nothing at all (stdout and stderr both
   empty) and each exits 0.

   print nothing and the tenth prints `irc:\nroom <A>: ...\n`. B never gets its own room lines.
4. **Limits, verbatim.** `irc_send` with 257 characters → `too long 257/256`; with cooldowns at 60 s a second room

   (`mairc config set`, which reloads the running daemon) → `pm off`. Each is a tool result with `isError: true`.
5. **Names are remembered.** B's shim exits; a new shim with the same `MAIRC_SEAT` initializes and `irc_read`
   works without calling `irc_name` again.
6. **Daemon restart.** Stop the daemon and start it again while A's shim stays up: A's next tool call succeeds

7. **No daemon.** With the daemon stopped, a hook run prints nothing, exits 0 and returns within 1 s.
8. **Claude format.** `mairc hook --client claude --event PostToolUse` with a pending private message prints one

   `--event UserPromptSubmit` it prints the plain text.

10. **HTTP transport.** A plain HTTP client posts `initialize` and `tools/call irc_name` to `/mcp` with the token

title: hook: `mairc hook`, zero output when nothing is new
description:
## Goal

`mairc hook`: the program an agent CLI's hook runs. It asks the daemon whether there is anything for this agent
right now. **If there is nothing, it prints nothing and exits 0, so the model spends zero tokens.** If there is
something, it prints only the new lines, in the form the agent CLI accepts.

This runs after every tool call of every agent. It must be fast, silent on every failure, and never block.

## Files you own

`internal/hook/*.go` (package `hook`), its tests, and `testdata/vectors/hook/*`. Nothing else. Standard library
only.

## What you build on

- `internal/config` (landed): `ResolvePaths`, `Load`, `ReadToken`; `Settings.Listen`, `Settings.HookTimeoutMS`.
- `internal/identity` (use it if landed, else take the values through `Options`): `identity.Seat(...)`,
  `identity.Ancestors(self, 8, identity.ParentOf)`.
- The daemon's hook endpoint, tested against a fake `httptest` server:
  `POST /v1/hook`, header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, body
  `{"pids":[...],"seat":"...","name":"...","event":"..."}`.
  `204` = nothing to deliver. `200` with `text/plain` = the lines to deliver, joined by `\n`.

## API to implement

```go
package hook

type Options struct {
	BaseURL string        // e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:4747"
	Token   string
	Timeout time.Duration // from Settings.HookTimeoutMS
	Client  string        // "claude" or "plain"
	Event   string        // --event; empty means: take hook_event_name from stdin JSON
	Name    string        // --name or $MAIRC_NAME; may be empty
```

```go
package install

type Options struct {
	Binary   string    // absolute path of the mairc binary to reference
	Scope    string    // "user" (default) or "project"
	Home     string    // the user's home directory
	Project  string    // the project directory (for scope "project")
	Print    bool      // --print: change nothing, write the snippets to Out
	Uninstall bool     // --uninstall: remove what install added

func Run(o Options) int
```

**1. MCP server**, merged into the JSON file for the scope (`<Home>/.claude.json` for `user`,

title: mcp: JSON-RPC 2.0 and the MCP subset, transport-free, with golden vectors
description:
## Goal

The MCP protocol core: JSON-RPC 2.0 and the small MCP subset `mairc` serves, with no transport in it. The daemon
calls it for each HTTP request; the shim forwards lines to it through the daemon.

## Files you own

`internal/mcp/*.go` (package `mcp`), its tests, and `testdata/vectors/mcp/*.json`. Nothing else. Standard
library only (`encoding/json`); **no MCP SDK**. The subset is small on purpose, so the wire behaviour stays ours
to keep tiny and to port.

## API to implement

```go
package mcp

// Server answers MCP messages for a fixed set of tools.
type Server struct{ /* unexported */ }

// New returns a server that serves tools under the given server name and version.
func New(name, version string, tools []core.Tool) *Server

// Handle processes one JSON-RPC message (a single request or notification; batches are refused) for a session.
// It returns the response bytes, or nil for a notification (nothing is sent back).
// It never returns an error: every failure is a JSON-RPC error response.
func (s *Server) Handle(ctx context.Context, sess *core.Session, msg []byte) []byte

// ToolListBytes returns the exact bytes of the tools/list result object, for the size test.
func (s *Server) ToolListBytes() []byte
```

`core.Tool`, `core.Session` and `core.ToolResult` are defined in `internal/core/core.go`:
a tool has `Name`, `Description`, `InputSchema` (compact JSON text) and
`Call(ctx, *core.Session, args []byte) core.ToolResult`; a result has `Text` and `IsError`.

## Protocol (MCP revision `2025-06-18`)

| Method | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `initialize` | result `{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"tools":{}},"serverInfo":{"name":<name>,"version":<version>}}`. If the client asks for another `protocolVersion`, still answer `2025-06-18`. |
| `notifications/initialized` | notification: return nil |
| `ping` | result `{}` |
| `tools/list` | result `{"tools":[{"name":..,"description":..,"inputSchema":{..}}, ...]}` in the order given to `New`; `inputSchema` is the tool's schema embedded as raw JSON |
| `tools/call` | params `{"name":"..","arguments":{..}}`; call the tool; result `{"content":[{"type":"text","text":<Text>}],"isError":<IsError>}`. Omit `isError` when false. Missing `arguments` means `{}`. |
| any other notification (no `id`) | return nil |
| any other request | error `-32601`, message `method not found` |

Errors (JSON-RPC `error` object, `id` echoed, or `null` when it could not be read):

- invalid JSON → `-32700` `parse error`
- not an object, a batch array, missing or wrong `jsonrpc`, missing `method` → `-32600` `invalid request`
- `tools/call` with an unknown tool name → `-32602` `unknown tool: <name>`
- `tools/call` whose `params` is not an object or whose `name` is missing → `-32602` `invalid params`

A tool that reports a problem is **not** a JSON-RPC error: it is a normal result with `isError: true`.

Output is compact JSON (no indentation), keys in the order shown, `id` echoed exactly as received (number or
string, including large numbers: keep it as `json.RawMessage`). Responses carry `"jsonrpc":"2.0"`.

## Golden vectors

Create `testdata/vectors/mcp/` with one file per case, each `{"in": <message>, "out": <response or null>}`:
`initialize`, `initialized-notification`, `ping`, `tools-list`, `tools-call-ok`, `tools-call-tool-error`,
`tools-call-unknown-tool`, `tools-call-bad-params`, `unknown-method`, `parse-error`, `batch-refused`,
`string-id`. Use two fake tools in the test (`echo`, which returns its `text` argument, and `fail`, which
returns an error result). The test runs every vector and compares bytes. A Rust port will run the same files.

## Tests

- every vector;
- `tools/call` passes the raw `arguments` bytes to the tool and the same `*core.Session` it was given, so a tool
  can change `Session.Name`;
- a notification returns nil; a request never does;
- `ToolListBytes` equals the `result` of the `tools-list` vector;
- fuzz target `FuzzHandle`: arbitrary bytes never panic and always produce valid JSON or nil.

## Not in this bead

HTTP, stdio, sessions' storage, the real tools (the `daemon`, `shim` and `tools` beads). No resources, prompts,
sampling, logging, progress, cancellation or SSE: they are out of scope for the project.

## Working rules (the same for every bead)

- **Project in three lines:** `mairc` is a tiny chat system for coding agents, served as an MCP server. A
  background daemon owns one SQLite file; agents reach it through a stdio shim, Streamable HTTP, and a hook that
  prints nothing when there is nothing to read. One public room, private messages, nothing else.
- **No scope creep.** Build exactly what this bead says. If something seems missing, write it in the bead's notes
  and ask; do not add features, flags, settings or dependencies.
- **Toolchain:** Go 1.27.4. `export PATH=$HOME/sdk/go1.27.4/bin:$HOME/go/bin:$PATH`. Build with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
- **Contract:** `internal/core/core.go` holds the shared types and interfaces. Use them as they are. Do not edit
  that file unless this bead says so.
- **Rust-port readiness:** standard library first; the only third-party dependency allowed in the whole project is
  `modernc.org/sqlite`, and only in `internal/store`. No reflection tricks, no code generation, no global mutable
  state, no `init()` side effects, no panics for control flow. Errors are values with stable short texts.
- **Tests:** table-driven, `testing` only (no assertion libraries), a fake clock, temporary directories, no
  sleeps, no network beyond loopback. Every user-visible string named in this bead is asserted verbatim.
- **Before you push:** `gofumpt -l . && go vet ./... && golangci-lint run && go test -race -count=1 ./...`, all
  clean. If `.golangci.yml` is not in the repository yet, run `golangci-lint run` with its defaults.
- **Stay in your files.** Touch only the paths listed under "Files you own". Remove the `.gitkeep` in a directory
  when you add its first real file.
- **Beads:** claim with `br update <id> --claim --actor "<model> (<your name>)"`, close with
  `br close <id> --reason "<commit> + the tests that prove it"`. Commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` with your work, name
  the bead id in the commit message, `git pull --rebase` then push to `main`.

## Goal

Agent names: the rule a name must satisfy, and a generator that makes names like `greenfox1` and `reddog7`.

```go
package names

// Valid reports whether name is acceptable: it matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,23}$ (2 to 24 characters, a lowercase

func Valid(name string) bool

// Check returns nil for a valid name and core.ErrNameInvalid otherwise.

// Normalize trims surrounding whitespace and lowercases ASCII letters. It does not make an invalid name valid.
```

title: identity: hardened seat — CLI session id, hostname, and the name learned from the hook event after irc_name
description:
## Goal

Make "which agent is this hook running for?" reliable everywhere: any operating system, any terminal, several
agents in one folder, agent CLIs that run their sessions under one shared background process, and (later) agents
on different machines talking to one daemon. Today the answer rests on the process chain and on a "seat" built
from tmux, the terminal or the working directory. Those can be missing or shared. This bead adds stronger keys in
front of them and keeps the old ones as fallbacks.

## The problem, concretely

- `mairc hook` is a fresh process per event. It must tell the daemon who it is without asking the model.
- Today the daemon resolves it in this order: an explicit `name`; a process id reported by a shim; the seat
  (`env:` from `MAIRC_SEAT`, `tmux:`, `tty:`, `cwd:`). See `docs/protocol.md` ("POST /v1/hook") and
  `internal/identity`.
- Where that fails: an agent CLI that runs many sessions under one shared process (the parent process id is the
  same for all of them and there is no terminal); three agents started in the same folder with no terminal
  information; two machines that both have a pane `%1` or a terminal `/dev/pts/3`.
- `docs/compat.md` ("What this means for mairc", point 2) records the better key: every hook-capable CLI passes a
  session id to the hook on stdin (`session_id`, `sessionId` or `conversationId`), and some also set it in the
  environment (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `GEMINI_SESSION_ID`, `GROK_SESSION_ID`).

## What to build (four parts, one change)

### 1. The hook reports its CLI session id

- In `internal/hook`: besides `hook_event_name`, read the session id from the stdin JSON: the first non-empty
  string among `session_id`, `sessionId`, `conversationId`. If stdin has none, use the first non-empty of the
  environment variables `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `GEMINI_SESSION_ID`, `GROK_SESSION_ID`.
- Accept it only if it is 1 to 200 characters of printable ASCII without spaces; otherwise treat it as absent.
- Send it to the daemon as a new optional field `session` in the `POST /v1/hook` body.
- `internal/shim` sends the same value as the header `X-Mairc-Session` on `initialize` **when one of those
  environment variables is set in the shim's own environment**. It often will not be; that is expected.

### 2. The daemon resolves by session first, and learns

New resolution order in `internal/daemon` (first that applies):

1. a non-empty `name` (unchanged);
2. `session`, when the daemon has that session bound to a name;
3. a process id reported by a shim, **on the same host** (part 3), when unambiguous (unchanged otherwise);
4. the seat (unchanged).

Learning: whenever a hook request carries a `session` and is resolved by rule 3 or 4, the daemon remembers
`session -> name`. From then on that session resolves by rule 2 even if the process chain or seat stops matching.
A shim that sent `X-Mairc-Session` binds it when its session gets a name.

**Bindings survive a daemon restart.** They are stored in the SQLite database the daemon already owns (not in a
separate file: the write is atomic with everything else and needs no second format):

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hook_session (
  session      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name         TEXT NOT NULL,
  last_used_ms INTEGER NOT NULL
) WITHOUT ROWID;
```

- Add three methods to `core.Store` (this bead may change `internal/core/core.go`; say so in the commit and
  add a line to `plan.md` §8 "Database"): `BindHookSession(ctx, session, name, now) error`,
  `HookSessions(ctx) (map[string]string, error)` and `PruneHookSessions(ctx, before time.Time) (int, error)`.
  Statements go in `internal/store/sql/queries.sql` like the others.
- The daemon keeps the bindings in memory too, loaded once at start with `HookSessions`, so the empty hook path
  still runs no SQL. A new binding is written to the database when it is made. `last_used_ms` is refreshed at
  most once an hour per session (in memory it is exact), never on every hook event.
- The one-minute retention pass deletes bindings unused for more than 7 days, in memory and in the table, so the
  table cannot grow without bound. A binding whose name no longer exists is dropped when it is next used.

A session bound to one name is never silently re-bound to another: if rule 3 or 4 later yields a different name
for a bound session, the binding wins.

### 3. The host is part of the seat and scopes process ids

- `identity.Seat` output becomes `<host>/<old seat>`, for example `buildbox/tmux:%12`. `<host>` is
  `os.Hostname()` lowercased, cut to 63 characters, with every character outside `a-z 0-9 . -` replaced by `-`;
  `unknown` if the call fails. `MAIRC_SEAT` values are prefixed too (`buildbox/env:grok-1`).
- The hook sends `host` in its body; the shim sends `X-Mairc-Host`. The daemon keys its process-id index by
  `(host, pid)`, so a process id from one machine never matches a shim on another.
- **Do not lose remembered names.** When a seat in the new form has no remembered name, the daemon also looks up
  the old form (the part after the first `/`) once, and if that has a name, binds the new-form seat to it
  (`UpsertAgent` already moves a name's seat). After that the old form is no longer consulted for that name.

### 4. The name is learned from the hook event that follows `irc_name`

This is what makes the shared-process, same-folder, no-terminal case work with no setup.

- Several CLIs pass the tool name and the tool's result to the hook that runs after a tool call (for Claude Code:
  `tool_name` and `tool_response` on `PostToolUse`). **Check `docs/compat.md` and each CLI's hook documentation
  for which CLIs do, and under which field names; list what you verified in a comment above the parser.**
- When the hook's stdin JSON shows that the tool just called was mairc's `irc_name` (the tool name ends with
  `irc_name`) and its result text matches exactly `you are <name>` with a valid name, the hook adds
  `"claimed":"<name>"` to its request.
- The daemon accepts a claim only when **all** of these hold: the request has a `session`; an `irc_name` call set
  or confirmed that exact name within the last 60 seconds; and that name is not already bound to a different hook
  session. Then it binds `session -> name`. Otherwise the claim is ignored and resolution proceeds as above.
- A hook that cannot see tool results simply never sends a claim; nothing else changes for it.

## What must not change

- The hook still prints nothing on stdout and stderr and exits 0 whenever nothing is due or anything fails.
- The empty hook path still does no database work for a hook resolved by name, session or process id.
- No new setting, no new tool, no new dependency. `MAIRC_SEAT` and `--name` keep working and keep their priority.
- Requests from an older hook or shim (no `session`, no `host`) are still served: missing fields mean "unknown",
  and an absent host matches only shims that sent no host.

## Files

`internal/identity` (seat format), `internal/hook` (stdin and environment parsing, new body fields),
`internal/shim` (two headers), `internal/daemon` (resolution, learning, host-scoped process ids),
`internal/core/core.go` and `internal/store` (the `hook_session` table and its three methods), `plan.md` §8,
`cmd/mairc` (pass the new values through), `docs/protocol.md` (the changed request and the resolution order),
`testdata/vectors/hook/` (new request vectors), `e2e/` (scenarios below). Update `skill/SKILL.md` and `README.md`
only if a sentence in them becomes wrong.

## Tests

Unit (fake daemon / `httptest`, no sleeps):
- hook: session id from each stdin field name, from each environment variable, stdin wins over environment,
  invalid ids dropped; `claimed` sent only for an `irc_name` result of the exact form; never for another tool,
  a malformed result or an invalid name;
- seat: host prefix, sanitising, the `unknown` fallback, `MAIRC_SEAT` still first;
- daemon: resolution order; learning from process id and from seat; a bound session survives a changed seat;
  a claim accepted inside 60 seconds and refused after, refused for a name bound to another session, refused
  without a `session`; process ids scoped by host; an old-form remembered seat is adopted once; old clients work.

End to end (real binary), each as its own test:
1. **Same folder, no terminal information, shared parent:** three agents whose hooks send only a session id
   (stdin JSON) and whose seat and process chain are identical. Each calls `irc_name`; the next hook event carries
   the tool name and result. A private message to each is delivered to that agent's hook and to no other.
2. **Session survives a moved seat and a daemon restart:** an agent resolved once by seat is still resolved
   after its seat changes, through its session id; and after the daemon is stopped and started again, the first
   hook event of that session, with a seat and process chain that match nothing, is resolved by the stored
   binding.
3. **Two hosts:** two agents with the same seat text and the same reported process id but different hosts do not
   receive each other's messages.
4. **Old client:** a hook request without `session` and `host` behaves exactly as before this bead.

## Done when

All of the above pass under `go test -race ./...`; `gofumpt`, `go vet` and `golangci-lint` are clean;
`docs/protocol.md` matches the code; the close reason lists, per CLI, which of the three mechanisms (session id,
claim from the tool result, fallback to process id or seat) was verified from documentation and which was verified
by a real run.

## Not in this bead

Letting agents on other machines reach the daemon (the listen address and a client-side server setting): that is
a separate, later bead. This bead only makes identity safe for it.
acceptance_criteria: The hook reports the CLI session id (stdin fields, then environment) and the daemon resolves by it before process id and seat, learning the binding; seats carry the host and process ids are matched per host, with remembered names adopted from the old seat form; a name is bound to a hook session from the irc_name tool result within 60 seconds under the stated conditions; older clients behave as before; the hook stays silent and database-free on the empty path; the four end-to-end scenarios and the unit tests pass under go test -race; docs/protocol.md matches; the close reason states per CLI what was verified from documentation and what by a real run.
notes: Landed c11acf5 on main. Differences from the bead text are listed in the commit message (machine inside the seat as @machine/place; a fresh claim moves the name; shim-reported session ids bind only while free; separate core.Bindings contract). Verification per CLI: session id fields and the PostToolUse tool_name/tool_response fields were taken from docs/compat.md (documentation and recorded hook input) for Claude Code, Codex, Devin, Grok, Gemini CLI and Antigravity; none was verified by a real run of a live CLI in this bead. The four end-to-end scenarios drive the real mairc binary with the JSON those CLIs document.
close_reason: Completed in c11acf5: session bindings (stored, survive restart), machine-qualified seats, name claim from the irc_name result; gate green (gofumpt, vet, golangci-lint 0 issues, go test -race). Field names verified from docs/compat.md only, not by live CLI runs.

title: shim: `mairc stdio`, the stdio-to-daemon MCP forwarder
description:
## Goal

`mairc stdio`: the program an agent's MCP configuration launches. It speaks MCP over stdio to the agent and
forwards every message to the daemon over HTTP. It keeps no chat state; it exists so that many agents share one
daemon while each still gets an ordinary stdio MCP server.

## Files you own

`internal/shim/*.go` (package `shim`) and its tests. Nothing else. Standard library only.

## What you build on

- `internal/config` (landed): `ResolvePaths(getenv) (Paths, error)`, `Load(path) (core.Settings, error)`,
  `ReadToken(path) (string, error)`; `Paths{Home, Config, DB, Token, Log, PID}`; `Settings.Listen` is the
  daemon's `host:port`.
- `internal/identity` (use it if landed; otherwise pass the seat and parent pid in through `Options` and let the
  `cli` bead fill them): `identity.Seat(...)`.
- The daemon's HTTP contract, which you test against a fake `httptest` server, **not** the real daemon:
  - `GET /healthz` → `200 ok`, no auth.
  - `POST /mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and one JSON-RPC message as the body.
    A request gets `200` and the JSON response as the body; a notification gets `202` and no body.
    The response to `initialize` carries the header `Mcp-Session-Id`; send it back on every later request.
    On `initialize` also send `X-Mairc-Seat: <seat>` and `X-Mairc-Pid: <pid of the agent process>`.
    `404` means the daemon no longer knows the session (it restarted).

## API to implement

```go
package shim

type Options struct {
	BaseURL   string            // e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:4747"
	Token     string
	Seat      string
	AgentPID  int               // the parent process id of the shim: the agent CLI
	In        io.Reader         // the agent's stdout -> our stdin
	Out       io.Writer         // our stdout -> the agent
	StartDaemon func() error    // starts the daemon detached; called when /healthz does not answer
	Client    *http.Client      // default: 10 s timeout
}

// Run forwards messages until In reaches end of file or ctx is cancelled. It returns nil on end of file.
func Run(ctx context.Context, o Options) error
```

## Behaviour

- **Framing:** MCP stdio is newline-delimited JSON: one message per line, no embedded newlines. Read lines of up
  to 1 MiB; write each response as one line followed by `\n`. Write nothing else to `Out`, ever: diagnostics go
  to stderr.
- **Start-up:** `GET /healthz` (500 ms timeout). No answer → call `StartDaemon`, then poll `/healthz` every 50 ms
  for at most 3 s. Still no answer → every request gets a JSON-RPC error (below); the shim keeps running and
  retries the health check on each new request.
- **Forwarding:** for each line, `POST /mcp`. Copy a `200` body to `Out` as one line. Write nothing for `202`.
  Messages are forwarded one at a time, in order.
- **Session:** remember the `Mcp-Session-Id` from the `initialize` response. Remember the raw `initialize`
  request line too.
- **Daemon restarted (`404`):** re-send the remembered `initialize` (discard its response, take the new session
  id), then re-send the failed message once. If that fails too, answer the error below.
- **Daemon unreachable or a non-2xx answer:** for a request (it has an `id`), write
  `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":<id>,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"mairc daemon unavailable"}}`; for a
  notification write nothing. The `id` is echoed exactly as received (keep it as raw JSON).
- A line that is not valid JSON is forwarded as it is; the daemon answers the parse error.
- **Exit:** end of file on `In` → return nil (the agent closed the server). The daemon is left running.

## Tests (fake daemon with `httptest`, `In`/`Out` as buffers or pipes)

- initialize then tools/list: both forwarded, headers correct (`Authorization`, seat and pid on initialize,
  session id afterwards), responses written one per line;
- a notification produces no output;
- daemon down at start: `StartDaemon` is called once, the shim proceeds when the fake comes up;
- daemon never comes up: a request gets the `-32000` error with its own id (number and string ids);
- restart: the fake answers `404` once; the shim re-initializes and the original request succeeds, with exactly
  one response line for it;
- a 1 MiB line passes; nothing but JSON lines is ever written to `Out`;
- end of file returns nil.

## Not in this bead

Starting the daemon process itself (`StartDaemon` is supplied by the `cli` bead), any chat logic, caching.

## Working rules (the same for every bead)

- **Project in three lines:** `mairc` is a tiny chat system for coding agents, served as an MCP server. A
  background daemon owns one SQLite file; agents reach it through a stdio shim, Streamable HTTP, and a hook that
  prints nothing when there is nothing to read. One public room, private messages, nothing else.
- **No scope creep.** Build exactly what this bead says. If something seems missing, write it in the bead's notes
  and ask; do not add features, flags, settings or dependencies.
- **Toolchain:** Go 1.27.4. `export PATH=$HOME/sdk/go1.27.4/bin:$HOME/go/bin:$PATH`. Build with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
- **Contract:** `internal/core/core.go` holds the shared types and interfaces. Use them as they are. Do not edit
  that file unless this bead says so.
- **Rust-port readiness:** standard library first; the only third-party dependency allowed in the whole project is
  `modernc.org/sqlite`, and only in `internal/store`. No reflection tricks, no code generation, no global mutable
  state, no `init()` side effects, no panics for control flow. Errors are values with stable short texts.
- **Tests:** table-driven, `testing` only (no assertion libraries), a fake clock, temporary directories, no
  sleeps, no network beyond loopback. Every user-visible string named in this bead is asserted verbatim.
- **Before you push:** `gofumpt -l . && go vet ./... && golangci-lint run && go test -race -count=1 ./...`, all
  clean. If `.golangci.yml` is not in the repository yet, run `golangci-lint run` with its defaults.
- **Stay in your files.** Touch only the paths listed under "Files you own". Remove the `.gitkeep` in a directory
  when you add its first real file.
- **Beads:** claim with `br update <id> --claim --actor "<model> (<your name>)"`, close with
  `br close <id> --reason "<commit> + the tests that prove it"`. Commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` with your work, name
  the bead id in the commit message, `git pull --rebase` then push to `main`.
acceptance_criteria: shim.Run forwards newline-delimited JSON-RPC to /mcp with the right headers, starts the daemon when it is down, re-initializes after a daemon restart and answers -32000 when the daemon is unreachable; nothing but JSON lines is ever written to the agent; tested against a fake daemon; lint, vet and race tests clean.
notes: Note from mairc-cli-nru (BoldLeopard, 17 Nov): shim.Options takes Token at start, but on a first run the daemon creates the token only when it starts, so the shim would send an empty token. cmd/mairc (b6be097) works around it: when the token is missing, stdio starts the daemon itself and waits up to 3 s for the token file before calling shim.Run. If the shim should own this (re-read the token after StartDaemon), that is a small API change for a later bead.

title: store: SQLite schema, statements and retention behind core.Store
description:
## Goal

The SQLite store: schema, statements and retention, implementing `core.Store`.

## Files you own

`internal/store/*.go`, `internal/store/sql/*.sql`, their tests, and `go.mod`/`go.sum` for the one dependency
`modernc.org/sqlite` (pure Go, no cgo). Nothing else.

## Contract to implement

`core.Store` in `internal/core/core.go` (read its doc comments; they are the specification of each method), with
the types `core.Message`, `core.Agent`, `core.Kind` and the error `core.ErrNameTaken`.

```go
package store

// Open opens (creating if needed) the database file, applies the schema and returns the store.
// Use path ":memory:" in tests only through OpenMemory.
func Open(path string) (*Store, error)
func OpenMemory() (*Store, error)
// *Store implements core.Store.
```

## Schema (`internal/store/sql/schema.sql`, embedded with `//go:embed`)

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent (
  name            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  seat            TEXT UNIQUE,              -- NULL when not bound to a seat
  last_seen_ms    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_public_ms  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_private_ms INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  room_cursor     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
) WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS message (
  id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  at_ms  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  sender TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('room', 'pm')),
  body   TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS message_room ON message (id) WHERE kind = 'room';
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS message_at ON message (at_ms);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS delivery (
  message_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES message (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  recipient    TEXT NOT NULL,
  delivered_ms INTEGER,                     -- NULL until read or delivered by a hook
  PRIMARY KEY (message_id, recipient)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS delivery_unread ON delivery (recipient) WHERE delivered_ms IS NULL;
```

Times are Unix milliseconds. `core.Agent` zero times correspond to 0.

## Behaviour

- **Connection:** `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=NORMAL`, `foreign_keys=ON`, `busy_timeout=2000`.
  One `*sql.DB` with `SetMaxOpenConns(1)`: all access is serialized, which is fast enough and keeps a Rust port
  simple (one connection behind a mutex).
- **Statements** live in `internal/store/sql/queries.sql` as named blocks (`-- name: InsertRoom` followed by the
  SQL). A small loader splits the embedded file by those markers; every statement is prepared once in `Open`.
- `UpsertAgent(name, seat, now)`:
  - new name → insert (seat `""` is stored as NULL);
  - existing name with the same seat, or with no seat, or called with seat `""` → update last-seen, and set the
    seat when one is given;
  - existing name bound to a **different** non-empty seat → `core.ErrNameTaken`;
  - when the seat is already bound to **another** name, that other agent's seat is set to NULL first (a seat has
    one name; taking a new name in a seat releases the old binding). Do both in one transaction.
- `InsertPM`: one `message` row and one `delivery` row per recipient, in one transaction; duplicate recipients are
  stored once.
- `UnreadPMs(recipient, now)`: select the undelivered messages oldest first and set `delivered_ms`, in one
  transaction, so two concurrent readers never both get a message.
- `RoomSince(after, exclude, limit)`: the **newest** `limit` room messages with `id > after` and
  `sender <> exclude`, returned oldest first.
- `RoomTail(limit)`: the newest `limit` room messages, oldest first.
- `Prune(now, keepHours, keepMessages)`: delete messages with `at_ms < now - keepHours*3600000`, then every
  message whose id is below the id of the `keepMessages`-th newest; delivery rows go by the cascade. Return the
  number of messages deleted.
- Every method takes `ctx` and uses the `...Context` database calls.

## Tests (against `OpenMemory()` and one file-backed case in `t.TempDir()`)

- each method's contract, including the four `UpsertAgent` cases and the seat hand-over;
- `InsertPM` to three recipients with one duplicate → three delivery rows;
- `UnreadPMs` returns each message once (call twice; second call is empty) and marks the time;
- `RoomSince` with more new lines than the limit returns the newest ones in ascending order and skips the
  excluded sender;
- `Prune` by age, by count, and both; delivery rows are gone afterwards;
- reopening a file-backed store keeps the data; `Open` twice on the same schema is harmless;
- a concurrency test: 8 goroutines inserting and reading under `-race`, no error, every message stored once.
- Benchmarks: `BenchmarkInsertRoom`, `BenchmarkHasUnreadPM` (report in the close reason).

## Not in this bead

Cooldowns, length limits, name rules, settings (the `chat`, `names` and `config` beads). The store stores what it
is given.

## Working rules (the same for every bead)

- **Project in three lines:** `mairc` is a tiny chat system for coding agents, served as an MCP server. A
  background daemon owns one SQLite file; agents reach it through a stdio shim, Streamable HTTP, and a hook that
  prints nothing when there is nothing to read. One public room, private messages, nothing else.

title: docs: agents on several machines through a port forward to one daemon (0.1.0, no code)
description:
## Goal

Document, for version 0.1.0, how agents on different machines of one private network (for example a Tailscale
tailnet) share one mairc daemon **with no code change**: each remote machine forwards the hub's port to its own
loopback and uses the hub's token. Write it only after proving it works with a real run.

## Why this works without code

- One machine (the hub) runs `mairc daemon`. It listens on loopback only (`127.0.0.1:4747` by default); the
  daemon refuses any other listen address, and that stays so in 0.1.0.
- On every other machine, `mairc stdio` and `mairc hook` talk to `http://<listen>` from their own `config.json`.
  If that local address is a tunnel to the hub's port, they reach the hub and behave exactly as if it were local.
- The daemon checks one bearer token, read by clients from their own data directory's `token` file. A remote
  machine therefore needs a copy of the hub's token file.
- Identity across machines is already safe once bead `mairc-seat-0fk` has landed: seats carry the host name and
  process ids are matched per host. **This bead depends on that one.**

## What to do

1. **Prove it.** On one machine, stand in for two: a "hub" home and a "remote" home (`MAIRC_HOME`), the remote's
   `listen` set to a different loopback port that forwards to the hub's port (an SSH local forward to the same
   machine, or any TCP forwarder you have). Copy the hub's `token` into the remote home. Then, with the real
   binary: an agent on each side takes a name, they exchange a room message and a private message, and each
   side's hook delivers once and is silent afterwards. If you have two real machines on a private network, repeat
   it across them and say so. Record the exact commands.
2. **Find the sharp edges and write them down**, each verified, not assumed:
   - what `mairc stdio` on the remote does when the tunnel is down (it tries to start a local daemon: does a
     local daemon then start on the forwarded port, and what happens when the tunnel comes back?). If this can
     split the chat into two daemons, the documentation must say how to avoid it (for example: keep the tunnel
     up as a service; or point `listen` at a port nothing local can bind);
   - the hook with the tunnel down: silent and fast (it must be, by design; confirm it);
   - `mairc status`, `mairc doctor` and `mairc config set` on the remote: which act on the hub and which on local
     files only;
   - the token: file permissions on the remote, and what to do when the hub's token changes.
3. **Write the documentation**:
   - `README.md`: a short section "Agents on several machines" (at most 25 lines): the picture in three
     sentences, the steps for the hub and for a remote machine with one worked example using a generic SSH local
     forward (`ssh -N -L 4747:127.0.0.1:4747 <hub>`), the sharp edges from step 2, and one line saying native
     support (no tunnel) is planned for 0.1.1.
   - `skill/SKILL.md`: one sentence at most, only if an agent needs to know anything (it probably does not:
     to an agent the chat looks the same). Keep the skill within its 1500-character limit.
   - `docs/protocol.md`: one paragraph stating that the daemon is loopback-only in 0.1.0 and that remote use is
     by port forwarding.

## Rules

- No Go code changes. If the proof in step 1 shows a real defect that makes this unusable, stop, describe it in
  the bead notes with the commands that show it, and ask; do not fix it here.
- This repository is public: no real host names, addresses, user names, tokens or network names in the text or
  in the commit. Use `<hub>` and example values.
- Do not recommend exposing the daemon's port on a non-loopback address by any other means (a reverse proxy,
  `socat` listening on all interfaces): the token is the only protection and the daemon was not designed for it.

## Done when

The proof run's commands and results are in the bead's close reason; the three documents are updated within their
limits; every statement about behaviour in them was observed in the proof run; `go test -race ./...` still passes
(nothing changed) and the README line count limit still holds.

title: remote: native multi-machine support — a non-loopback listen address behind allow_remote, and a client-side server setting (0.1.1)
description:
## Goal (version 0.1.1, deferred: do not start before 0.1.0 is released)

Let agents on other machines of a private network (for example a Tailscale tailnet) use one mairc daemon directly,
without a port forward.

## What exists

- 0.1.0 supports this only through a tunnel to the hub's loopback port (README, "Agents on several machines").
- The daemon refuses any non-loopback `listen` address (`internal/config` validation).
- `mairc stdio` and `mairc hook` derive the daemon's address from the local `listen` setting, and `mairc stdio`
  starts a local daemon when it cannot reach one.
- Identity is already safe across machines (bead `mairc-seat-0fk`: host in the seat, process ids per host).

## What to build

1. **Hub side:** allow `listen` to be a specific non-loopback address of this machine (for example its tailnet
   address), never a wildcard (`0.0.0.0`, `::`), behind an explicit second setting `allow_remote` (default
   false). With `allow_remote` false the validation stays exactly as it is.
2. **Client side:** a new setting `server` (`host:port`, default empty). When set, the shim, the hook, `status`,
   `doctor` and the reload after `config set` talk to it; the shim never starts a local daemon and answers its
   daemon-unavailable error when the hub is unreachable.
3. **Token:** document how to give a remote machine the hub's token. No new mechanism.
4. **Tests:** unit tests for both settings' validation; an end-to-end test with two homes where the "remote" one
   has `server` set; the hub refusing a wildcard address; the shim not starting a daemon when `server` is set.
5. **Docs:** replace the tunnel instructions with the native ones and keep the tunnel as an alternative.

## Not in this bead

TLS, accounts, hub-to-hub syncing, discovery of hubs. The private network provides the encryption and the reach.
acceptance_criteria: With allow_remote false nothing changes; with it true the daemon accepts one specific non-loopback address and refuses wildcards; with server set, the shim, hook, status, doctor and config reload use it and the shim never starts a local daemon; the two-home end-to-end test passes; docs updated.
notes: From the 0.1.0 docs proof (f1a951f): on a machine that reaches the hub through a forward, a shim started while the forward is down starts a local daemon on that port and splits the chat. Native support should let a machine be marked as a client of a remote daemon so that mairc stdio never starts a daemon there.

title: tools: the four MCP tools (irc_name, irc_send, irc_read, irc_who), token-lean
description:
## Goal

The four MCP tools agents use, on top of `core.Chat`. They are the whole surface an agent sees, so they are
written to cost as few tokens as possible: short names, one-line descriptions, plain-text results.

## Files you own

`internal/tools/*.go` (package `tools`), its tests, and `testdata/vectors/tools/*`. Nothing else.

## Build against the contract

Use `core.Chat`, `core.Tool`, `core.Session`, `core.ToolResult`, `core.Message` and the `core.Err...` values from
`internal/core/core.go`. **Write a fake `core.Chat` in your test file**; do not import `internal/chat`.

```go
package tools

// All returns the four tools, in this order: irc_name, irc_send, irc_read, irc_who.
func All(chat core.Chat) []core.Tool
```

## The tools (every string below is served verbatim and asserted by a test)

| Name | Description | Input schema (compact JSON) |
|---|---|---|
| `irc_name` | `Set your chat name, or omit name to get one.` | `{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}}}` |
| `irc_send` | `Send to the room, or privately: to="a,b".` | `{"type":"object","properties":{"text":{"type":"string"},"to":{"type":"string"}},"required":["text"]}` |
| `irc_read` | `Unread private messages and the last n room lines.` | `{"type":"object","properties":{"n":{"type":"integer"}}}` |
| `irc_who` | `Names seen recently.` | `{"type":"object"}` |

## Behaviour

Each tool's `Call(ctx, sess, args)` parses `args` (a JSON object; empty or `null` means `{}`), calls the chat
layer with `sess.Name` and `sess.Seat`, and returns a `core.ToolResult`.

- **`irc_name`**: `chat.SetName(ctx, name, sess.Seat)`; on success set `sess.Name` to the returned name and
  answer `you are <name>`.
- **`irc_send`**: `to` is split on commas and whitespace, empty parts dropped; no `to` (or only separators) means
  the room. `chat.Send(ctx, sess.Name, recipients, text)`; success answers `sent`.
- **`irc_read`**: `chat.Read(ctx, sess.Name, n)`; answer one `Message.Line()` per message joined by `\n`
  (`pm greenfox1: hello` / `room reddog7: hello`); no messages → `nothing new`.
- **`irc_who`**: `chat.Who(ctx)`; answer the names joined by one space; none → `nobody yet`.
  `irc_who` works without a name.
- **Errors**: any error from the chat layer becomes `ToolResult{Text: err.Error(), IsError: true}`. The texts
  come from the chat layer unchanged (`no name: call irc_name`, `cooldown 42s`, `too long 300/256`, `empty`,
  `unknown: bob,carol`, `pm off`, `room off`, `too many recipients (max 16)`,
  `bad name: use a-z, 0-9, _ or -, 2-24 chars, letter first`, `name taken`).
- **Bad arguments**: args that are not a JSON object, or a field of the wrong type (`text` not a string, `n` not
  an integer) → `ToolResult{Text: "bad arguments", IsError: true}`. Unknown fields are ignored.
- A tool never panics and never returns an empty `Text`.

## Token budget (the point of this bead)

- A test builds the `tools/list` result object exactly as MCP serves it,
  `{"tools":[{"name":..,"description":..,"inputSchema":..},...]}` in compact JSON, and asserts it is
  **at most 1200 bytes**. Save it as `testdata/vectors/tools/tools-list.json` and compare byte for byte, so any
  growth is a visible diff.
- No tool result has a preamble, a trailing newline, JSON, markdown, timestamps or ids.

## Tests

- the table above, verbatim, and the order of `All`;
- each tool: success text, each error text passed through with `IsError`, bad arguments;
- `irc_send` recipient parsing: `"a,b"`, `"a, b"`, `"a b"`, `" a ,, b "`, `""` → room;
- `irc_name` updates `sess.Name`; a failed `irc_name` leaves it unchanged;
- `irc_read` formatting with private and room messages in the order given by the chat layer;
- the size test and the golden file.

## Not in this bead

The rules themselves (cooldowns, limits: the `chat` bead), JSON-RPC (the `mcp` bead), transports.

## Working rules (the same for every bead)

- **Project in three lines:** `mairc` is a tiny chat system for coding agents, served as an MCP server. A
  background daemon owns one SQLite file; agents reach it through a stdio shim, Streamable HTTP, and a hook that
  prints nothing when there is nothing to read. One public room, private messages, nothing else.
